# beowulf-fitt-36 — cruces worth recording in QUESTIONS.md

Each: line · word · what was chosen · why disputed or guessed.

- 2605 · `heregrīman` · dative singular "under the war-mask" (helmet with face-guard); the ending could be dative plural of a weak noun.
- 2606–08 · `folcrihta gehwylc` · "each of the folk-rights"; practical sense (a landholder's standing and dues) is a guess.
- 2612 · `Ōhtere[s]` · genitive supplied from Grundtvig's translation; MS `ohtere` (Thorkelin `Oþeres`); `suna` read as genitive singular of the u-stem.
- 2613 · `wræcca(n)`, `Wēohstān` · (n) from Ettmüller/Schücking; italic n: MS `weohstanes` (genitive would make Wēohstān the victim), Grundtvig's `Wēohstān` followed.
- 2615 · `brūnfāgne` · "brown-gleaming" (guess; Thorkelin's transcript `hasufāgne`); `hringde byrnan` kept in MS order (Rieger/Holthausen `byrnan hringde`).
- 2618–19 · `nō ymbe ðā fǣhðe spræc … hē his brōðor bearn ābredwade` · subject of `spræc` taken as Onela, `hē` of the concession as Wēohstān, `brōðor bearn` as Ēanmund; `ābredwade` "struck down" (rare verb).
- 2620 · `[ðā]` · supplied (Grundtvig, Ettmüller, Sievers, Holthausen); `ǣrfæder` taken as the father (or a forefather), a guess.
- 2628 · `mǣges` · MS `mægenes`; E.Sc. `mǣges` "kinsman's" = Ēanmund's sword, followed; `hīe` = Wīglāf and dragon (guess).
- 2629 · `þæt` · MS `þa` ("then"); Thorpe `þæt` followed.
- 2636 · `gūðgeatwa` · MS `getawa`; italic at; sense unchanged.
- 2638 · `Ðē … þē` · taken as "because"; no main clause (the reasons pile up to 2646).
- 2640 · `onmunde ūsic mǣrða` · hapax-like verb; "took thought of us for glories" is a guess; Bugge `ond mēda gehēt` for `ond mē þās māðmas geaf`.
- 2642 · `ūs` · dative "for us"; E.Sc./Thorpe/Bugge `ūser`, Grundtvig `ūre`, Aant. `ūr`.
- 2646 · `dollīcra` · "daring" (guess at tone; the word can mean "rash").
- 2649–50 · `hyt sŷ glēdegesa grim` · `hyt` kept as "it"; Kemble `hit [hāt]`, Thorpe/Sedgefield `hāt`, Grein `hit` "heat"; `glēdegesa` for `-egsa` (Sievers, Holthausen).
- 2650 · `God wāt on mec` · `on` "concerning" a guess; `mid` + accusative; `fæðmię` ending read as subjunctive -e.
- 2654–55 · `mægen`, `fāne` · `mægen` read as subjunctive of `magan` (not the noun); `fāne` taken as accusative of `fāh` used as noun (form shorter than `fāgne`).
- 2657 · `nǣron ealdgewyrht` · plural verb with no stated subject; read "it is no due of his old deeds".
- 2659 · `ūrum … bām` · MS `urū` with `ð` over the line and `ð·sceal·` in the margin; Thorpe/Grein `unc`, Sedgefield `hūru`.
- 2660 · `beaduscrūd` · MS `byrdu scrud`; Aant./Holthausen `bord` for `byrne`.
- 2661 · `wīgheafolan` · "war-head" = helmet (lexica); sense of `bær … on fultum` follows.
- 2671 · `nīos(i)an` · MS B `niosnan`, A `mosum`; Kemble/Holthausen/Schücking `nīosan`, Grein `nīosian`; `fāh` "gleaming" over "stained".
- 2673 · `bord wið rond[e]` · -e from Kemble; "burned up to the rim" is a guess.
- 2676 · `w(æs)` · restored from Grundtvig's translation.
- 2678 · `m(ǣrða)`, comma after `gemunde` · Grundtvig restoration; Rieger/Holthausen put the comma after `slōh`.
- 2680–81 · `Nægling` · etymology from `nægl` is a guess.
- 2684–87 · `wæs sīo hond tō strong, sē ðe …` · parenthesis (Schücking, Holthausen, Chambers); `sēo` (Thorpe); `þone` for `þonne` (Bugge, Holthausen); `ofersōhte` "overtaxed" a guess; `wund[r]um` (MS `wundū`) "wondrously" vs "with wounds".
- 2688 · `Þā wæs … rǣsde` · `wæs` has no clear construction; read as an impersonal frame ("it was the third time"); `þā him rūm āgeald` "when room repaid him" is a guess; `biteran bānum` ending odd; `ymbe-`/`ymb-` (Thorpe, Trautmann, Holthausen).
